title: Vintage teddy bear too fragile to stitch, rebuilt with cotton backing
description: This vintage jointed teddy bear's fur had become so brittle that every stitch opened another hole. He was taken apart, washed, and every piece was lined with fusing web and cotton backing. With new strength hidden inside, his holes were closed, and he was restuffed and rejoined.
itemDetails: This is a vintage jointed teddy bear with short golden-brown plush, rounded ears and a black moulded nose. His head, arms and legs are attached to the body with internal disc joints, so each one can turn. No maker's label was found, so the brand and exact age have not been identified.
repairDetails: This bear arrived with tears and holes all over his body, and his neck had split open with the old stuffing showing through. His fur fabric had become brittle and very fragile. Whenever one hole was stitched, stretching the fabric opened another one, so surface stitching alone could never hold him together. Every piece needed backing fabric underneath. Because he is a jointed bear, his head, arms and legs were separated from the body at the joints, the old stitching was unpicked, and all of the old stuffing was removed. The body fabric was washed first, then the limbs. Fabric glue went onto the weakest areas. Iron-on fusing web was bonded to the back of the old fabric, and a layer of cotton was ironed on top. The body seams were then closed on the sewing machine. Paper patterns were made to fit his curved head, and the head was lined piece by piece in the same way. With cotton supporting the fur from inside, the holes and tears could finally be stitched closed and the stitches held. He was restuffed, his head and limbs were rejoined and tightened, the last openings were closed by hand, and he was finished with a blue ribbon.
